messages.author: 375745764f4199d6
messages.subject: inla.mode options
parts:
Dear INLA experts,

I am using the latest stable version of INLA and I have noticed that the results between the models implemented defining inla.mode as "compact", "classic" or "twostage" are quite different. Could someone be so kind to briefly explain to me the differences between the three options? I have not found any documentation about it.

Furthermore, searching in this discussion group, it seems that there is also a fourth option ("experimental") not mentioned in R-help. Was it used only in the previous version of the package?

Thank in advance for your time.
Best regards,
Chiara

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla.mode options
parts:
with newer versions (since mid-December 2022), you should not be needed
to set or care about that option.


'experimental' is identical to 'compact'

'twostage' was an intermedidate step, that we were able to bypass.

'classic' is the old implementation as described in the 2009 paper.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla.mode options
parts:
inla.hyperpar is for 'classic' only.

for the default mode, there is not way to improve the hyperparameters
estimates.

we're working on a series of variational Bayes corrections, and we have
done the mean (default), variance (not default) and we're working on the
skewness for the latent field. Next one after that is
hyperparameters....
